title: A stalled registered test run has no supported cancel or timeout, so it holds its WinB slot indefinitely
outcome: A stalled registered test run has no supported cancel or timeout, so it holds its WinB slot indefinitely
acceptance: A registered test run (foreground, background or detached) can be stopped through a supported launcher or host route by its owner or coordinator. The stop ends the run's whole process tree and records a terminal 'cancelled' result that frees its slot. It needs no process kill by hand and no process listing.
A run whose output has stopped beyond a documented liveness bound can be ended through that same supported route. The bound must not decide pass/fail for a slow but progressing run.
Behavioural tests start a real child tree that hangs and show that the cancel route ends it and records the cancelled result, on Windows and on POSIX.

completion.summary: Shipped supported per-run launcher cancellation for an owner or coordinator, including a stall-scoped stop requiring a current episode. Native Windows jobs and POSIX process groups reap the owned process tree, terminal results distinguish confirmed cancellation from unresolved cleanup, and stall/advisory timing cannot fail progressing work. Exact exclusive Windows FULL passed and the independent evaluation passed all three criteria. Master was fast-forwarded to the exact gated commit and independently confirmed. Integration reports installation pending for its next batch and the running host still awaits Greg's restart.
